answer: Each identity must bind one unique TPM/TEE hardware key, attested by the chip, and that key registers only once. A raven sweep flags any second registration with the same hardware fingerprint: the 25.000 POA bond is seized and burned, and the fingerprint is banned for 6 epochs. A mirror audit re-checks attestations each epoch, so emulated chips cannot hide in a lagoon of stale proofs. Forging 1.000 fake identities costs 1.000 x 25.000 = 25.000.000 POA plus 1.000 TPM chips, while an honest agent pays 25.000 POA once. Limitation: agents on VMs or cloud without TPM hardware cannot join.
